label: Cause of the received totality: primitive cause of the esse of all received bearers together
term: cause of the esse of the received totality
definition: TotalityCause e is an explicitly PRIMITIVE predicate parameter: e is a cause of the esse of the totality of received actual bearers (ReceivedActual p) taken together, in the same esse respect as CausesIn. It is a cause of the whole collection's being actual, not the distributive fact that each member has some cause. It is constrained only by the premises that use it: an actual such cause exists if anything is received (A), and it causes the esse of each received member (B). Nothing else, including its position inside or outside the totality, is assumed.
note: Primitive relation under the encode-first primitive rule, analyst formulation for #1724 (C1), attribution deferred; the Lean declaration named is the first premise that constrains the parameter. Distinguishing conditions: (i) not the plurality of member causes (the Hume-Edwards regress control has every member caused and no totality cause); (ii) not a law, abstract configuration or global obtaining fact unless that item is an actual bearer of the profile; (iii) not identified with the spacetime-whole cause of NaturalismConsequences (#1109), whose vocabulary and whole differ. Ordinary-language examples: a cause of a whole run of printed copies being in existence, as opposed to the fact that each copy was copied from an earlier one; counterexamples: an idle actual explainer that supplies no member (control 4) satisfies A without B. Structural properties assumed: none (no irreflexivity, uniqueness or externality). Open semantic obligations: whether any real causal relation satisfies A and B at the fixed esse respect, and whether a totality of received being is a proper explanandum (the Hume-Edwards rival denies it). Dependencies: e7aa4529-fe7a-4baf-929c-466cf15cb0c6, 211a6432-8b8f-53ed-85e3-75173bb15b24 (cause of a perfection), DEF-ESSE.
